title: Founding of the League of Nations
summary: The League of Nations came into being on 10 January 1920, when the Treaty of Versailles took effect. Headquartered in Geneva, it was created after the First World War as a forum for resolving international disputes, drawing on theories of collective security. Woodrow Wilson first proposed it in his Fourteen Points, yet the United States never joined. Its plans included procedures for arbitration and mechanisms for economic and military sanctions.

uncertainty.note: The League began on 10 January 1920, when the Treaty of Versailles came into effect.

as_recorded.value: The League of Nations began life on 10 January 1920, when the Versailles Peace Treaty, signed in 1919 to formally end the First World War, came into effect.
The League of Nations was an international organization, headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland , created after the First World War to provide a forum for resolving international disputes.

importance.justification: An early international organization for settling disputes between states after the First World War.

related.because: Part I of the Treaty of Versailles contained the Covenant of the League of Nations that formally established the organization upon ratification.
The catastrophic destruction of the First World War led the victorious Allied powers to establish a permanent collective security body to prevent future global conflicts.

reviewer_note: The date marks when the League began, not when it moved to Geneva. The pin is the city of Geneva, its headquarters. The sources opened do not call it the first organization of its kind, so the summary does not either.
